title: Bodhi Tree - The Sacred Tree of Enlightenment
content:
Bodhi Tree

The Bodhi Tree in Bodh Gaya, Bihar, is one of the most sacred places in the world. It is the site where Prince Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment and became Lord Buddha. This tree stands as a timeless symbol of peace, wisdom, and spiritual awakening, drawing millions of pilgrims and visitors every year.

History and Significance

Over 2,500 years ago, Siddhartha meditated under the original Bodhi Tree for several days, achieving the ultimate truth - enlightenment. The present tree is believed to be a descendant of that original tree, carefully preserved through generations. It represents hope, faith, and the search for inner peace.

Architecture and Surroundings

The sacred tree stands inside the Mahabodhi Temple complex, surrounded by a peaceful garden, meditation areas, and ancient stone railings. Near the tree lies the Vajrasana (Diamond Throne) - the exact spot where Buddha sat during his meditation. The tranquil setting inspires meditation and reflection among visitors.

Best Time to Visit

The best time to visit the Bodhi Tree is from October to March, when the weather is cool and pleasant, perfect for meditation and sightseeing.

How to Reach

  • By Air: Nearest airport - Gaya International Airport (12 km)
  • By Train: Nearest railway station - Gaya Junction (16 km)
  • By Road: Easily accessible by buses and taxis from Patna, Rajgir, and Nalanda.

Entry Fee and Timings

  • Entry Fee: Free for all visitors
  • Timings: 5:00 AM - 9:00 PM (open daily)

Tips for Visitors

  • Maintain silence and respect the spiritual atmosphere.
  • Avoid touching or damaging the sacred tree.
  • Try to meditate under the tree for a few minutes of peace.
  • Visit early morning or evening for a calm experience.
